text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault not seen giving up on effort to block merger between Guinness and GrandMet despite their rejection on Friday of his proposals to merge the three companies' wines and spirits activities. Analysts say he could bbost his stake in GrandMet. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- Paris court to choose this week among bidders for hotels group Royal Monceau.
-- U.S. media group CBS interested in buying a 49 percent stake held by Alcatel in TV channel Euronews, for which British group ITN-Reuter is also expected to bid.
-- LVMH, signalling greater flexibility in its negotiating position, may accept as little as 25 percent in a company merging its wine and spirits activities with those of Guinness and GrandMet.
-- Government project to create some 350,000 jobs for young people to be reviewed this week.
-- A 20 billion franc recapitalisation for insurer GAN expected to be approved by European authorities on Wednesday.
-- Guinness and GrandMet seen threatening to raise to 50 percent of votes the level needed to block their merger in an effort to thwart LVMH.
